answer: Sequential bridge permits: each agent identity must carry a unique record of a verified cross-chain bridge transfer, signed by the destination chain's kernel. Registration accepts a record only once; replaying or duplicating it fails a nullifier check. To mint N identities, an attacker must perform N distinct real bridge transfers, each paying bridge fees and finality latency, so cost scales linearly with identity count. The ivory rule: permits expire after one epoch and cannot transfer between agents, forcing continuous genuine activity.
